question: Following Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) in an adult patient who remains comatose, which ONE of the following is the most appropriate immediate management priority?

answers.text: Administer a bolus dose of adrenaline to maintain systolic BP above 100 mmHg

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Bolus adrenaline post-ROSC risks precipitating ventricular arrhythmias. Haemodynamic support uses vasopressors/inotropes titrated by infusion, not boluses.

answers.text: Maintain normothermia or targeted temperature management (32–36°C) and normoglycaemia

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Current post-resuscitation care prioritises targeted temperature management (avoiding hyperthermia ≥37.8°C, with many centres targeting 32–36°C), normoglycaemia (4–10 mmol/L), and haemodynamic optimisation.

answers.text: Extubate the patient immediately if they follow commands

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Comatose patients cannot follow commands and require ongoing airway protection. Even partially responsive patients should be assessed carefully before extubation post-arrest.

answers.text: Withhold 12-lead ECG until the patient is haemodynamically stable for 30 minutes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A 12-lead ECG should be obtained immediately post-ROSC to identify STEMI or other reversible cause; percutaneous coronary intervention should not be delayed.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Post-Resuscitation Care section. The key post-ROSC priorities are temperature management, normoglycaemia, haemodynamic support, and rapid coronary angiography if indicated.
Correct. The post-arrest syndrome is managed with targeted temperature control, normoglycaemia, haemodynamic optimisation, and urgent coronary intervention if STEMI is present.
